from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Sweep-Line Logic", [

            "Rotation triggers swapping two adjacent points.",

        ])

        # Setup visualization
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(color=BLUE) for _ in range(3)])

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Brute force checks all pairs.", "Sweep-line remembers point order.", "This significantly reduces operations."]
        self.setup_layout("Complexity & Efficiency", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for the lecture lines (must only change colors)
        l1, l2, l3 = self.lecture[0], self.lecture[1], self.lecture[2]
        
        # Animation Elements
        comp_formula = MathTex(r"O(N \log N)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(comp_formula, 'B2')
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 5, 1], x_length=3, y_length=3)
        graph_n2 = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2/5, color=YELLOW)
        graph_nlogn = axes.plot(lambda x: x*np.log(x+1)/2, color=BLUE)
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, graph_n2, graph_nlogn)
        self.place_at_grid(graph_group, 'E3')
        
        bar_chart = BarChart([1, 0.2], bar_names=["Brute", "Sweep"], y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.2], x_length=3, y_length=2)
        self.place_at_grid(bar_chart, 'D5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(l1.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Write(comp_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(l2.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), Create(graph_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(l3.animate.set_color("#00FF00"), Create(bar_chart))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion & Real-world Application", [
            "Crucial for convex hull algorithms.",
            "State management drives geometric solutions.",
            "Efficiently navigates complex 2D maps."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Summarize algorithm steps
        box = SurroundingRectangle(self.lecture[0], buff=0.1, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(box))
        
        steps = VGroup(
            Text("1. Sweep Line", font_size=20),
            Text("2. Event Queue", font_size=20),
            Text("3. Update Status", font_size=20)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_at_grid(steps, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(steps), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(box))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show real-world example: collision detection
        robot = Circle(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=1)
        obstacle = Polygon(LEFT*0.3+UP*0.3, RIGHT*0.3+UP*0.3, RIGHT*0.3+DOWN*0.3, LEFT*0.3+DOWN*0.3, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(obstacle, 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        path = Line(self.grid['D3'], self.grid['D5'], color=YELLOW)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(robot), FadeIn(obstacle))
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight key takeaways
        takeaways = Text("Geometric Algorithms = State Management", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(takeaways, 'F3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(takeaways))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Windmill Problem (Computational Geometry & Sweep-Line Algorithm)
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Computer Science or Mathematics

sections.title: Introduction: The Setting
sections.content: Define the problem: N points on a plane. A line passes through one point (the pivot). The line rotates like a windmill arm until it hits another point. That new point becomes the new pivot. Visualize this as a 'bouncing' rotation.
sections.example: Imagine N fireflies in a dark room. A light beam pivots on one firefly, rotating until it strikes the next, transferring the pivot like a baton in a relay race.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Angular Sorting
sections.content: Explain that the order of 'hits' depends on the angles of vectors. Introduce the concept of cross-products to determine the orientation (clockwise/counter-clockwise) without calculating trigonometric functions.
sections.example: Visualizing two vectors from the pivot: using the sign of the cross-product to decide which vector has a smaller angle relative to the current rotation direction.

sections.title: The Sweep-Line Logic
sections.content: Explain the state maintenance: We keep an array of points sorted by their current angular position relative to the pivot. As the line rotates, only two adjacent points in this sorted order swap places when the line hits them.
sections.example: An animation showing a sorted list [P1, P2, P3] changing to [P2, P1, P3] as the line sweeps past the alignment of P1 and P2.

sections.title: Complexity & Efficiency
sections.content: Discuss why this is efficient (O(N^2 log N) or O(N^2) with optimization). Compare the brute-force approach (checking all pairs) vs. the sweep-line approach (updating sorted order).
sections.example: A comparison table: Brute force involves N^3 checks; our optimized approach 'remembers' the sequence, drastically reducing operations.

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-world Application
sections.content: Summarize how this solves problems related to convex hulls and point-set triangulations. Emphasize that geometric algorithms are just clever ways of managing state changes.
sections.example: Application: How robots use this logic to navigate around static obstacles in a 2D map to find the shortest path.
